reviewMethod: Primary publication/university/museum reading; Commons original-file metadata through MediaWiki imageinfo and revision API; visual inspection of all 20 local reference photographs. No independent taxonomic expert review.

sources.title: Qu’est-ce qu’un blob ?
sources.scope: Physarum polycephalum: plasmodium, sexual fusion, sporulation and germination.
sources.limits: Museum overview; no universal timing, mating-type count or field identification rule is imported.

sources.title: Physarum: a plasmodial slime mold — Inanimate Life
sources.scope: Structure of a multinucleate plasmodium and sexual-cycle order.
sources.limits: Used for biology, not as a source of photographs or the current taxonomic placement.

sources.title: Slime Mould Facts
sources.publisher: University of Warwick, School of Life Sciences
sources.scope: Amoeboid/flagellate forms, cysts, fusion and reversible plasmodial sclerotium.
sources.limits: Group-level educational account illustrated with Physarum. Its resting branch is not evidence that any pictured Arcyria specimen formed a sclerotium.

sources.title: Mycosphere Essays 3. Myxomycete spore and amoeboflagellate biology: a review
sources.scope: Spore germination; feeding/dividing myxamoebae; alternative flagellate and cyst phases; sexual fusion and nuclear division without cell division.
sources.limits: Typical heterothallic pathway; the review explicitly describes other nuclear cycles. Swimming forms are not described as dividing without first reverting to amoebae. No blanket species-level mating claim.

sources.title: Agar Cultivation of Myxomycetes Arcyria denudata (L.) Wettst. — A potential source of secondary metabolites
sources.scope: Species description and cultured germination, myxamoebae, white veined plasmodium and sporocarps; figure 2 and Results, p.48.
sources.limits: A single cultivation report, not a field timing model. The cultured sporocarps were poorly developed and stalkless, unlike the field description. We do not generalize the paper’s durations, temperatures, colour changes or morphology to every individual. Fusion and resting branches are supported separately at group level. No images reproduced from this paper.

sources.title: Sporophore morphology and development in the myxomycetes: a review
sources.scope: Sporocarps, sporangia, stalks, spore-bearing structures; resistant sclerotium versus sporulation; environmental variation in sporocarp form.
sources.limits: Anatomical terminology only. Historical classification in the review is not adopted as a current classification tree; Ceratiomyxa’s external spore formation is not merged into these cycles.

sources.title: Multigene phylogeny of the order Physarales (Myxomycetes, Amoebozoa): shedding light on the dark-spored clade
sources.scope: Badhamia polycephala, new combination, MycoBank MB 846262; basionym Physarum polycephalum, p.113.
sources.limits: The atlas retains the educational/source name Physarum polycephalum and discloses the new combination, without changing source determinations or constructing an unsourced phylogeny.

sources.title: NCBI Taxonomy: Badhamia polycephala
sources.scope: Database currently displays Badhamia polycephala and the basionym Physarum polycephalum.
sources.limits: Corroborating database, not the sole nomenclatural authority; see the primary revision above.

physarum.scope: Simplified sexual-cycle example for Physarum polycephalum (Badhamia polycephala).
limits: The stages are an order, not elapsed time.
Photos are different specimens; no morphing or slideshow is observational time-lapse.
Amoeboid and swimming cells are alternatives; microcysts are distinct from the plasmodial sclerotium.
Other reproductive routes exist and are outside this simplified sexual path.

arcyria.scope: General heterothallic myxomycete pattern, explicitly contextualized for Arcyria denudata.
limits: The cultivation paper supports germination, amoebal cells, plasmodial growth and fruiting, not every illustrated transition.
Fusion and sclerotium are group-level explanations, not observations of the photographed individuals.
No verified reference photograph of the Arcyria plasmodium is in the local collection.
The pale arcyria-detail image is excluded as a stage reference.

illustrationGuidance.type: Clearly labelled educational illustration, including any generated artwork; never a reference photograph.
illustrationGuidance.spore: Schematic cell and protective wall; surface sculpture and physical scale are not calibrated.
illustrationGuidance.cells: Show amoeboid and flagellated forms as alternatives, not two obligatory successive stages. A microcyst is a resting unicellular form.
illustrationGuidance.fusion: Two compatible cells and their nuclei unite in the sexual pathway; do not show a many-cell aggregation or Dictyostelium slug.
illustrationGuidance.network: One multinucleate plasmodium; nuclei are symbolic. Yellow Physarum imagery must not be treated as observed Arcyria anatomy or colour.
illustrationGuidance.fruit: Physarum and Arcyria have separately depicted sporocarps. A sporocarp contains many spores; its size is not the size of a spore.
illustrationGuidance.rest: Optional plasmodial sclerotium branch returning to plasmodium; never present it as an obligatory stage after fruiting.

photoObservations.note: The original observation discusses mature sporocarps. Its current name differs from the historical Commons file label; the nomenclatural relation is verified in the 2023 paper.

The observer suggests that white, cottony and brown forms may be successive stages. This is a hypothesis, not a verified developmental series, so the pale file is not assigned to an early or resting stage.

limits: All Russian common names are descriptive teaching labels, not verified official vernacular names.
Commons file names and community determinations are preserved as source labels, not promoted to expert verification.
New atlas entries describe only visible features and pictured substrate, not a complete species diagnosis, distribution or diet.
Species names are not a sourced contemporary classification tree; family/genus relationships are not inferred from visual similarity.
Original metadata may contain uncertainties and spelling differences, including Lycogala epidendrium in one source description; these are preserved here.
Generated art and renderer integration are handled separately; this registry does not claim those images have passed a scientific visual review.
No physical-device test or expert microscopy was performed.
